description:
Proposed works include a hip to gable end roof extension, a full size loft conversion including a rear dormer extension to accomodate a new primary bedroom and a front porch extension for a clock room.

The site previously obtained planning permision for a rear ground floor and first floor extension (Reference: PP-12146374). We will be making some minor amendments in regards to design and the previously obtained planning permission. The amendments include changing the proposed ground floor and first floor roof form to a flat roof proposal. This will allow a more practical and functional proposal for the proposed loft dormer extension.
decision_conditions:
<p>

<span pt="" sans=""></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-top: 5pt; margin-right: 0cm; margin-bottom: 0.0001pt;">The
proposed rear dormer extension, by reason of its excessive width and &nbsp;lack of visual containment, and the and first
floor rear flat roof, by reason of its poor and unsympathetic design, would
result in an unduly obtrusive and incongruous addition that would poorly relate
to the existing dwellinghouse and that would appear visually cramped,
detracting from the character of its semi-detached pair and out of keeping with
properties in the surrounding area. The rear dormer and first floor rear flat
roof would thereby unacceptably harm the character of the original
dwellinghouse and the visual amenities of the area, contrary to the high
quality design aspirations set out in The National Planning Policy Framework
(2024), policies D3 (D(1) and D(11)) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS1.B on
the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Development Management Local
Plans Policies (2013) and Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design
Guide (2010).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p>The proposal, by reason of the site being
located within an area of land liable to flooding and the lack of a
comprehensive Flood Risk Assessment, due to a lack of up to date flood maps/data
and flood mitigation measures, has failed to demonstrate that the proposed
development would not exacerbate the risk of flooding within the site or
increase the risk and consequences of flooding elsewhere, contrary to the
National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy SI12 of The London Plan
(2021), Core Policy CS1.U of Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and Policy DM 9 of the
Harrow Development Management Polices Local Plan (2013).</p>
